title: Robotaxis drive miles just to get cleaned and charged; this new startup wants to fix that
author: [[Kirsten Korosec]]
description: Aseon Labs, which came out of Y Combinator's 2026 spring cohort, has raised $10 million from Crane Venture Partners and others.

title: OpenAI limits GPT-5.6 rollout after government request, says restrictions shouldn’t be the norm
author: [[Rebecca Bellan]]
description: “We don’t believe this kind of government access process should become the long-term default,” says OpenAI. “It keeps the best tools from users, developers, enterprises, cyber defenders, and global partners who need them.”

title: Why everyone from OpenAI to SpaceX is building their own chips (and turning up the heat on Nvidia)
author: [[Theresa Loconsolo]]
description: Nvidia has dominated the AI chip market for years, but the era of total dependence might be ending.   OpenAI just shared its plans to spice things up with Jalapeño, its custom inference chip built with Broadcom, joining Google, Apple, and SpaceX in a growing list of companies building their way out of single-supplier risk. title: FTC gives Musk the OK to acquire SpaceX alumni startup Mesh
author: [[Marina Temkin]]

title: Corgi, the buzzy Y Combinator-backed insurance tech startup, says it didn’t steal an open source product
author: [[Julie Bort]]
description: Corgi became embroiled in controversy when Papermark accused it of stealing its software. Corgi says it did not, raising new questions about vibe coding.

title: It’s not about Anthropic vs. OpenAI anymore
author: [[Russell Brandom]]
description: AI models have progressed to the point where their capabilities have real political consequences. Dealing with those consequences will require collective action.
